narrative.overview:
A clean sportswear-retail storefront in which the team's own finished kit is the product on the shelf. The ground is white; royal blue arrives as full-bleed field panels at the top of every page and in the ordering band; black is the utility bar, the primary button and the footer. Real ODM mockups do the selling: they sit on the blue panel or on a pale wash, lift off it with one soft shadow, and on Home, Browse Designs and Contact an object (mockup or contact card) overhangs the panel's bottom edge into the white page below.

Type is all Jost: light-weight uppercase display set big, tracked uppercase labels, and calm mixed-case body. One handwritten accent, Mrs Saint Delafield, names the kit or the idea it sits beside. Red is a signal, never a field: hairline rules, the active-nav underline, hover and focus. Everything is square-cornered. The system refuses the dark, flame-and-neon "athletic" template.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, royal-blue field panels, black utility bar, buttons and footer.
Jost light uppercase display, tracked uppercase labels, one script accent.
Red only as hairlines, active-nav underline, hover and focus.
Square corners everywhere; 1px and 1.5px lines carry structure.
One soft drop-shadow family under mockups and overhanging cards.
Real mockups at or below natural size; logos exactly as supplied.

rules.name: The Red Is a Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Red is never a panel, card, text block or large fill. It appears as hairlines (the 56 x 3px rule, 1.5px underlines), the active-nav underline, hover states (including the primary button's hover fill) and the focus ring. If red covers an area at rest, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Blue Is a Field Rule
rules.body: Royal blue is used as a full-bleed panel or as small accents on white (numerals, tags, icons, script). It never becomes a button fill; on blue, buttons are black primary or white outline.

rules.name: The Script Ground Rule
rules.body: The Mrs Saint Delafield accent is white on the royal blue panel and where it crosses a saturated photo (Home hero "Aurora Vega"). On light grounds (white or the wash) it is royal blue, as on the Contact "Names & numbers" caption. It is never set over pale photo areas. One script line per view, decorative only (aria-hidden or doubled by real text).

rules.name: The Light Caps Rule
rules.body: Display is Jost 300 uppercase; weight comes from size, not boldness. Bold (600) appears only as the emphasised half of a headline.

rules.name: The Natural Size Rule
rules.body: A real mockup is never displayed wider than its natural pixel width (the Home hero is capped at 560px for a 630px source; gallery frames stay under the 975 to 1200px sources). Frames share one aspect ratio (979 / 923) so captions align; images fill with object-fit cover, never upscaled.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only mockups and overhanging cards cast a shadow, and only this soft family. Buttons, nav, panels, chips and text never do.

rules.name: The Logos As Supplied Rule
rules.body: The chrome wordmark, varsity badge, O-M mark and tagline lockup are placed exactly as supplied: cropped only, never redrawn, recolored, outlined, shadowed or restyled.

dos: Do open every page with the black utility bar, white nav and a royal-blue panel holding a Jost 300 uppercase display title.
Do put a 56 x 3px Signal Red rule above every section headline.
Do set the script accent white on blue or over a saturated photo, and royal blue on white or wash.
Do let one real mockup or card overhang the blue panel's bottom edge, carrying the overhang shadow.
Do show mockups at or below their natural width, in the shared 979 / 923 frame on the wash ground.
Do keep every corner square and draw structure with 1px and 1.5px lines.
donts: Don't use Signal Red as a fill, panel or running-text color; at rest it appears only as hairline rules and the active nav or filter, otherwise only on hover and focus.
Don't set the script over pale photo areas, or use more than one script line per view.
Don't add rounded corners, extra shadow styles, or shadows on buttons, panels or text.
Don't upscale a mockup past its natural pixel width.
Don't redraw, recolor, outline or restyle any ODM logo; use it exactly as supplied.
Don't use dark, flame, neon or gradient "athletic" treatments.
